battle.title: Graph Architect
battle.description: Design the map: matrices, lists, degrees and who is connected to whom.

questions.text: Which graph representation always uses O(V^2) memory, however few edges there are?
questions.explanation: A matrix stores one cell per vertex pair. An adjacency list stores only the edges that exist, O(V + E).
The graph is undirected, so edge {0,1} also adds 0 to vertex 1's list, followed by neighbours 2 and 3. Printing [2, 3] forgets the reverse direction of the first edge.

questions.text: A road network has 100000 junctions and about 200000 roads. You must list the neighbours of a junction quickly. Which representation fits?
options: An adjacency matrix of 100000 x 100000 booleans
A list of all roads scanned for every query
questions.explanation: The graph is sparse, so a list uses about 400000 entries (2 per road). A matrix needs 10^10 cells, far too much memory, and scanning every road is O(E) per query.

questions.text: An undirected graph with E edges is stored as an adjacency list. How many entries are there in total across all lists?
options: 2E, because each edge appears in both endpoints' lists
questions.answer: 2E, because each edge appears in both endpoints' lists
questions.explanation: Edge {u,v} is stored once under u and once under v. In a directed graph the total would be E.

questions.text: These edges are directed (from, to). What does the program print for the in-degrees?
questions.explanation: In-degree counts edges arriving at a vertex: vertex 1 receives from 0, 2 and 3, vertex 2 from 0. Counting the first number instead gives the out-degrees [2, 0, 1, 1].

coding.title: Sorted Neighbour Lists
coding.description: Build an adjacency list for an undirected graph with n vertices numbered 0 to n-1. For each vertex from 0 to n-1 print the vertex, a colon, and then its neighbours in increasing order, each preceded by a space. A vertex with no neighbours prints just the colon. There are no self loops and no repeated edges.
coding.inputDescription: Line 1: n and m. Then m lines, each with two vertices u v (an undirected edge).
coding.outputDescription: n lines in the form 'v: a b c'.
